chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Zurara, who said:
I asked him (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram, can he cover himself? He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for [covering] from the heat and the cold, then no.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.يَتَغَطَّى: To cover oneself (specifically the head in this context)

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram cover their head to protect against heat or cold?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* through the chain of Zurarah, this hadith clarifies that the prohibition of covering the head during Ihram is specific to protection from environmental elements like heat and cold, distinguishing it from other forms of covering. This ruling underscores the principle of simplicity and detachment from worldly comforts during the pilgrimage state, a key theme in Shia fiqh regarding the sanctity of the ritual boundaries.
